sources.entry: Uguu - Stores files and deletes after X amount of time. MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: Uguu is a lightweight temporary file hosting and sharing platform (also usable as a permanent file host) written in PHP, with uploads compiled by Bun.
summary.what_it_does: Uguu provides one-click file uploads with no registration, and a minimal web interface that supports drag-and-drop and paste. It has an upload API that can respond in JSON, HTML, plain text, or CSV, and the README says it works with ShareX and other screenshot tools. Administrators can set file extension and MIME black/whitelists, upload rate limits, and file hash blacklisting. The README says it was tested with Nginx, PHP 8.3, and SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL. Bun is used to compile the front end, after which the app runs on PHP.
how_to_run: Installation and configuration are described in the external Uguu Documentation (the README does not include commands).
notable: Upload API with JSON, HTML, text, and CSV response formats
Works with ShareX and other screenshot tools
File extension, MIME, and file-hash blacklisting plus upload rate limiting
No registration required; drag-and-drop and paste uploads
Forked from Pomf, the project it credits as its basis
caveats: Installation details are only in external documentation, not the README
README does not state how long temporary files are kept; the awesome-selfhosted listing describes deletion after a set time
